newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies called lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies called lower.

text.p: CME live hog and pork belly futures were called lower at the opening, with hogs expected down 0.25 to 0.50 cent per lb and pork bellies down 0.50 to 0.75 cent, analysts said.
Expected lower cash hog prices at Midwest markets Wednesday plus another drop in cash pork prices late Tuesday should spark continued selling in CME hogs and pork bellies.
CME hogs closed Tuesday down the 1.50-cent-per-lb daily limit in October and December and more selling was expected Wednesday by traders unable to fill sell orders Tuesday.
Late Tuesday, USDA reported pork cutout values were down $0.64 to $0.56 per cwt, with cash loins down $2.00 to $130.00 for 14- to 22-lb portions.

Also, bearish for hog and pork belly futures was Tuesday's USDA Cold Storage Report, which showed an 18.3-million-lb increase in total frozen pork supplies from September 1 to October 1. The frozen total amount of pork bellies in storage was considered neutral to futures.
"This is purely a case of high prices rationing demand," said one analyst of the increase.
